title: How to Hide a Security Camera: 15 Creative Spots That Work
excerpt: 15 proven locations to hide security cameras inside and outside your home. Specific spots, installation tips, and product recommendations for each location.
author: HiddenCameras Editorial
body:
Hiding a security camera is both an art and a science. The goal is placement that captures the right angle while remaining undetectable to visitors, intruders, or anyone else who might be recorded. Whether you are monitoring your home for security, checking on pets, or keeping an eye on a rental property, the right hiding spot makes the difference between a camera that works and a camera that gets found.

This guide covers 15 proven hiding spots — 8 indoor and 7 outdoor — with specific product recommendations for each location. Every spot has been tested for camera visibility, field of view, and practical installation considerations.

Indoor Hiding Spots

1. Bookshelf Integration

Best camera: Wyze Cam v3 or Blink Mini 2

Why it works: A bookshelf gives you natural cover and elevation. Place the camera between books at eye level, facing the room. The books provide camouflage from multiple angles, and the camera is at the perfect height for facial recognition.

Installation tip: Use a small piece of double-sided tape to secure the camera. Face it between two books so only the lens is visible. The Wyze Cam v3 is small enough to fit between standard hardcover books. Position it so the lens sits just past the book edges — enough to see the room, not enough to be obvious.

What it captures: Full room view at face height. Excellent for living rooms, home offices, or entryways.

2. Decorative Plant Placement

Best camera: Blink Mini 2 or Wyze Cam v3

Why it works: A potted plant on a shelf or table provides natural concealment. The leaves break up the camera silhouette, and people do not scrutinize plants. Place the camera behind leaves with a clear line of sight to the room.

Installation tip: Use a plant with dense foliage — a pothos, fern, or artificial plant works well. Position the camera so 2-3 leaves partially obscure the body but leave the lens exposed. The plant should be at a height that captures faces, not just the tops of heads.

What it captures: Concealed view of the room with natural-looking cover. Good for living rooms and bedrooms.

3. Smoke Detector Mount

Best camera: Hidden camera smoke detector (dedicated unit)

Why it works: A smoke detector is the last place anyone looks for a camera. It is high on the ceiling, has a natural reason to exist, and its round shape provides 360-degree coverage of the room below.

Installation tip: Replace your existing smoke detector with a hidden camera version. Mount it in the same location — typically center of the room or hallway. Make sure the new unit still functions as an actual smoke detector for safety.

What it captures: Overhead view of the entire room. Excellent for monitoring large spaces.

4. Bookend or Figurine Mount

Best camera: Mini spy camera or Wyze Cam v3

Why it works: A decorative bookend or figurine with a camera built in or hidden behind it provides excellent concealment. The object looks normal on a shelf or desk, and the camera is positioned at the perfect height for capturing people in the room.

Installation tip: Choose a bookend or figurine that faces the room naturally. If using a standalone mini camera, place it behind the object with the lens peeking around the side. Secure with a small piece of putty or tape.

What it captures: Desk-level or shelf-level view of the room. Good for home offices or entryways.

5. Tissue Box Mount

Best camera: Mini spy camera or Blink Mini 2

Why it works: A tissue box on a coffee table or desk is completely unremarkable. Nobody questions a tissue box. Place the camera inside the box with the lens positioned at the opening where tissues come out.

Installation tip: Remove tissues from the top layer, place the camera inside facing outward through the tissue opening, and replace a few tissues to partially conceal the lens. The camera captures everything in front of the box at table height.

What it captures: Table-level view of the room. Excellent for living rooms, offices, or reception areas.

6. Picture Frame Mount

\p>

Best camera: Frame-shaped hidden camera

Why it works: A picture frame on a wall or shelf provides a natural housing for a camera. The frame has a reason to exist, is at the right height, and faces the room directly. Nobody examines picture frames for hidden lenses.

Installation tip: Mount the frame at eye level (5-6 feet) facing the area you want to monitor. If using a frame with a built-in camera, make sure the lens is positioned in the upper corner of the frame where it would be least noticeable. For standard frames, place a mini camera behind the frame with the lens protruding slightly.

What it captures: Direct face-level view of anyone in the room. Ideal for entryways and hallways.

7. Curtain Rod Mount

Best camera: Mini spy camera or Blink Mini 2

Why it works: The top of a curtain rod, near the ceiling, provides an elevated vantage point that covers the entire room. The curtains themselves provide cover, and the camera is high enough that casual observation will not spot it.

Installation tip: Use a mini camera with a clip or adhesive mount. Attach it to the curtain rod bracket or the rod itself, facing into the room. Position it behind the curtain fabric so only the lens protrudes. The elevation gives you a wide-angle view of everything below.

What it captures: Wide overhead view of the room. Good for monitoring large spaces or rooms with high foot traffic.

8. Electrical Outlet Mount

Best camera: Outlet-hidden camera (dedicated unit)

Why it works: A wall outlet is one of the most overlooked objects in any room. A hidden camera disguised as an electrical outlet or placed adjacent to one is virtually undetectable. The outlet is at the right height for capturing faces and has a natural reason to exist on any wall.

Installation tip: Use a dedicated outlet-hidden camera that replaces or covers the existing outlet. Position it at eye level (4-5 feet) facing the main traffic area. Some models include night vision and motion detection.

What it captures: Face-level view of anyone entering or moving through the room. Ideal for entryways, hallways, and offices.

Outdoor Hiding Spots

9. Birdhouse Mount

Best camera: Blink Outdoor or Wyze Cam Outdoor

Why it works: A birdhouse mounted near your front door or backyard provides a natural, elevated vantage point. The birdhouse looks completely normal, and the camera can be positioned inside or behind it with the lens facing the area you want to monitor.

Installation tip: Mount the birdhouse at 8-10 feet high, facing the walkway or yard. Use a weatherproof outdoor camera inside the birdhouse with a small hole cut for the lens. The elevation provides a wide-angle view and makes the camera extremely difficult to spot.

What it captures: Elevated outdoor view of your property. Excellent for front yards, backyards, and driveways.

10. Outdoor Light Fixture

Best camera: Floodlight camera or light fixture hidden camera

Why it works: An outdoor light fixture is expected, has power, and is positioned at a height that captures faces. Nobody questions a light fixture on the exterior of a house. Many modern floodlight cameras combine lighting and surveillance in one unit.

Installation tip: Replace your existing porch light with a floodlight camera unit, or position a mini camera inside an existing light fixture. The camera benefits from the light source for night vision and captures anyone approaching your door.

What it captures: Front door and porch area with integrated lighting. Ideal for monitoring visitors and deliveries.

11. Garden Decoration Mount

Best camera: Mini outdoor camera or Blink Mini with weatherproof housing

Why it works: Garden gnomes, decorative rocks, planters, and other yard decorations provide perfect cover for outdoor cameras. The camera can be placed inside or behind the decoration, facing the area you want to monitor.

Installation tip: Choose a decoration that faces the target area naturally. Cut a small hole for the lens or position the camera behind the decoration. Secure with weatherproof adhesive. The decoration should be elevated enough to capture faces, not just feet.

What it captures: Ground-level or mid-height view of your yard or garden. Good for monitoring specific areas like gates or back doors.

12. Tree Mount

Best camera: Blink Outdoor or Wyze Cam Outdoor

Why it works: A tree provides natural elevation, cover from leaves and branches, and a vantage point that covers a wide area. Mounting a camera on a tree at 8-12 feet high gives you a surveillance angle that is very difficult to detect.

Installation tip: Use a weatherproof strap or mounting bracket to secure the camera to the trunk. Position it facing the area you want to monitor. The tree bark and surrounding foliage provide natural camouflage. Aim for a tree that overlooks your driveway, backyard, or property boundary.

What it captures: Wide outdoor view from an elevated position. Excellent for monitoring large properties or property boundaries.

13. Mailbox Mount

Best camera: Mini outdoor camera or Blink Mini 2 with weatherproof housing

Why it works: Your mailbox is at street level, faces your home, and is in a location where delivery people and visitors naturally approach. A camera inside or on the mailbox captures everyone who comes to your door.

Installation tip: Place a mini camera inside the mailbox facing outward, or mount one on the back of the mailbox facing your home. The mailbox provides natural cover, and the camera is at the perfect height for capturing faces. Make sure the mailbox still functions for actual mail delivery.

What it captures: Street-level view of your front yard and anyone approaching your home. Ideal for monitoring deliveries and visitors.

14. Fence Post Mount

Best camera: Blink Outdoor or Wyze Cam Outdoor

Why it works: Fence posts provide natural mounting points at a consistent height along your property boundary. A camera mounted on a fence post covers the area beyond your fence — sidewalk, street, or neighboring property.

Installation tip: Mount the camera on the post facing outward from your property. Use a weatherproof mounting bracket. Position it at 6-8 feet high to capture faces while remaining above casual observation. The fence post provides a stable, permanent mounting point.

What it captures: Property boundary view. Good for monitoring sidewalks, streets, or areas beyond your fence line.

15. Roof Eave Mount

Best camera: Any weatherproof outdoor camera

Why it works: The eaves of your roof provide a sheltered, elevated mounting point that covers your entire property. Cameras mounted under eaves are protected from weather, and the height makes them nearly impossible to spot from ground level.

Installation tip: Mount the camera under the eave at the corner of your house, facing the yard or driveway. The overhang protects the camera from rain and sun. Use a weatherproof camera with a wide-angle lens for maximum coverage. The height (10-15 feet) gives you a comprehensive view of your property.

What it captures: Wide overhead view of your entire property. The best option for comprehensive outdoor surveillance.

General Tips for Hiding Security Cameras

Elevation matters. Mount cameras at 6-10 feet high. Below 5 feet, they are easy to spot. Above 12 feet, they lose facial recognition detail. The sweet spot is 7-9 feet — high enough to be unobtrusive, low enough to capture clear faces.

Face traffic patterns. Position cameras to capture the faces of people entering or moving through the area. Cameras facing walls or ceilings record the tops of heads — not useful for identification.

Use natural cover. Leaves, books, decorations, and existing objects provide better concealment than artificial covers. People do not scrutinize objects that naturally belong in a space.

Test before finalizing. Mount the camera temporarily first. Check the live feed to verify the angle, field of view, and visibility. Adjust before permanent installation.

Consider power and Wi-Fi. A hidden camera is useless if the battery dies or the Wi-Fi signal is weak. Plan your power source and test Wi-Fi strength at the hiding spot before installation.
